name: Lazarus Street RipDoc Full Surgical Rig
description:
Ash-white poly-sealed surgical coat, hem cut asymmetrically to clear digitigrade legs or tail mods, over a moisture-wicking antimicrobial underlayer in pale green. Reinforced cuffs seal tight against chrome wrists; the back panel unzips into a sterile drape. Cargo trousers with instrument loops and an integrated knee pad — for crouching over a patient on a Shelf floor. Scuffed mag-closure boots with fluid-barrier soles.

A battered AR visor mounted on a worn headband serves as surgical display. Nitrile-analog gloves are permanently clipped to the left breast pocket. Nothing matches. Everything works.
functionality: Fluid-barrier coat and boots, sterile drape back panel, chrome-wrist sealed cuffs, AR surgical visor mount, instrument cargo loops, tail/digitigrade hem clearance, and antimicrobial underlayer for infection control in non-sterile environments.
what_it_says: You fix people that the licensed clinics turned away, and you haven't lost one yet — at least not to your mistakes.
story_hooks: The coat's serial number traces back to a Pellucid BioSeal licensed surgical set — reported stolen from a Tier 4 gene clinic three years ago.
A ripperdoc in this kit is the only person in the Shelf who knows how to remove a specific brand of corporate tracker implant.
The AR visor still has the previous owner's patient files cached — including someone very powerful who needed very quiet surgery.
